title: Dedicated staged rollouts: stage definition UX + API contract (weights, approvals, eval windows, default gates)
creator: Marissa Cole
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Define the v1 stage definition UX and the API contract for Dedicated staged rollouts. This ticket is the source-of-truth for:
- the fields we expose in Console (wizard + edit flows)
- the fields we support in control plane + public/operator APIs (create/update/approve)
- default stage templates + default gates for beta

Context
Dedicated pools are high-SLA and capacity-constrained. A stage definition must:
- express deterministic traffic allocation to candidate vs baseline within a single Dedicated pool
- include evaluation windows and minimum time-in-stage
- support manual approvals (with RBAC) and safe, auditable transitions
- configure gates with sane defaults while keeping advanced config behind an “advanced” disclosure

Out of scope (v1)
- multi-armed bandit or adaptive allocation
- per-request semantic/quality gating for all customers (may be optional/limited)
- customer self-serve for all Dedicated tenants (operator-only + enterprise opt-in for beta)

Primary users
- Redwood operators (SRE/release engineering) performing model/runtime/config changes on Dedicated pools
- Enterprise customer operators (opt-in) with approval permissions

Links
- Confluence PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/dedicated-staged-rollouts-prd.json
- Console UX spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-ux-staged-rollouts-dedicated.json
- ADR (gate evaluator): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-027-dedicated-rollout-gate-evaluation.json
- ADR (approvals + audit): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-028-rollout-approvals-and-audit-logging.json

Requirements
A) Stage definition UX (Console)
1) Stage list UI must allow defining an ordered set of stages.
   - Required: stage name, traffic split (candidate %), evaluation window, min duration, approval policy.
   - Must validate: monotonic progression of candidate traffic (e.g., 0 -> 5 -> 25 -> 100), unless explicitly overridden (advanced).
   - Must validate: candidate percent is integer 0–100.
2) Provide v1 templates:
   - “Standard (Safe)”: Shadow (optional) -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%
   - “Fast”: 10% -> 50% -> 100%
   - “Single step”: 100% (for emergency/low-risk changes)
3) Advanced settings behind disclosure:
   - custom gates per stage
   - custom hold/rollback actions
   - metric freshness policy (defaults apply; see below)
4) Stage-level summary:
   - show required approval(s) and who can approve (based on RBAC)
   - show which gates apply and their thresholds

B) API contract (control plane + operator API)
We need a stable schema that Console + internal tooling can use. Names below are not final; intent is.

Entity: RolloutPlan (Dedicated)
- rollout_plan_id (string, server-generated)
- tenant_id (string)
- pool_id (string)
- target (string): what is being rolled out (e.g., model version, runtime version, config bundle). v1 can treat as opaque “candidate_release_ref”.
- baseline_release_ref (string)
- candidate_release_ref (string)
- created_by (actor)
- updated_by (actor)
- plan_version (int) for optimistic concurrency
- state (enum): DRAFT | ACTIVE | PAUSED | ABORTED | COMPLETED
- stages (ordered list)
- default_gate_set_id (optional string) OR inline default gates applied to all stages unless overridden

Entity: Stage
- stage_id (string, server-generated)
- name (string)
- order_index (int)
- mode (enum): LIVE | SHADOW
  - LIVE: real traffic is split baseline vs candidate
  - SHADOW: requests are mirrored to candidate but responses are not served (best-effort), and do not count toward customer-facing latency SLOs; gating uses candidate-side metrics only where available
- candidate_traffic_percent (int 0–100)
  - Interpretation: percent of eligible requests routed to candidate within this pool.
  - Baseline receives 100 - candidate_traffic_percent.
- allocation (enum): DETERMINISTIC_HASH
  - Deterministic hashing required to avoid per-request flapping.
- evaluation_window_seconds (int)
  - The window used for gate aggregation once the stage is in “EVALUATING”.
- min_stage_duration_seconds (int)
  - Minimum time in stage before auto-advance can occur (even if gates are green).
- warmup_seconds (int, default 120)
  - Time after entering stage before we start evaluating gates (avoid cold-cache/initialization noise).
- approval_policy (enum): MANUAL | AUTO
  - MANUAL: requires explicit approval to enter stage (and optionally to exit/advance; see below)
  - AUTO: can advance automatically when gates pass
- approval_required_to_enter (bool)
- approval_required_to_advance (bool)
  - Proposed v1 default: enter requires approval for first LIVE stage; advance requires approval only when candidate_traffic_percent >= 25% (configurable by template).
- max_time_in_stage_seconds (int, optional)
  - If exceeded: action = HOLD (default) to force operator intervention.

Entity: Gate (per stage)
- gate_id (string, server-generated)
- type (enum): P95_LATENCY | ERROR_RATE_5XX | TIMEOUT_RATE | QUEUE_DEPTH | GPU_UTILIZATION
- query_scope (enum): POOL | ROUTE (v1 default POOL to control cardinality)
- threshold (string)
  - Stored as string to allow typed parsing (e.g., “p95_ms<=800”, “rate<=0.5%”, “depth<=50”). Backend owns validation.
- comparator (enum): LTE | GTE
- evaluation_period_seconds (int) (should match or be <= stage evaluation window)
- failure_action (enum): HOLD | ROLLBACK
  - v1 recommended default: HOLD for latency/queue depth/util; ROLLBACK for sustained 5xx/timeouts (see defaults below)
- require_fresh_metrics (bool, default true)
- metrics_max_age_seconds (int, default 180)
  - If metrics are older than this, evaluator must fail safe (HOLD) and surface “metrics stale” reason.
- consecutive_failures_to_trigger (int, default 2)
  - Avoid single-sample flake.

Entity: Approval
- approval_id (string)
- stage_id (string)
- action (enum): APPROVE_ENTER | APPROVE_ADVANCE | ABORT | ROLLBACK | RESUME
- actor (string)
- actor_type (enum): USER | SERVICE
- reason (string, optional)
- created_at (timestamp)

C) Default gates (beta recommendations)
Defaults should be stage-specific (stricter at higher traffic) but keep v1 simple. Proposal:
- Gate set applied to LIVE stages by default:
  1) P95_LATENCY (POOL): p95_ms <= baseline_p95_ms * 1.20 OR absolute ceiling (e.g., 900ms). (Open question: relative-to-baseline support in v1; if not, use absolute default thresholds per pool tier.)
  2) ERROR_RATE_5XX (POOL): 5xx_rate <= 0.5% (action: ROLLBACK for sustained failures)
  3) TIMEOUT_RATE (POOL): timeout_rate <= 0.5% (action: ROLLBACK for sustained failures)
  4) QUEUE_DEPTH (POOL): queue_depth <= 50 (action: HOLD)
  5) GPU_UTILIZATION (POOL): util <= 90% (action: HOLD)
- Stage timing defaults (template):
  - warmup_seconds: 120
  - evaluation_window_seconds: 600 (10m)
  - min_stage_duration_seconds: 900 (15m)
- Missing/stale metrics must fail safe:
  - evaluator sets stage status = HOLD with reason “metrics missing/stale”
  - no automatic advancement allowed while any required metric is stale

Acceptance criteria
- A single spec (this ticket + linked Confluence page) lists the exact required fields for stage creation/editing in Console.
- Engineering confirms which fields will be first-class in control-plane schema vs derived defaults.
- UX and API definitions are aligned: every required Console input maps to an API field, default, or server-derived value.
- Validation rules defined (percent bounds, stage order, approval policy constraints).
- Default gates defined for beta with clear note of what’s configurable vs fixed in v1.
- Open questions explicitly listed with owner + decision date.

Open questions
1) Relative-to-baseline thresholds: do we support baseline comparison in v1 (requires baseline query + join), or ship absolute thresholds per pool tier?
2) Shadow stage semantics: do we allow Shadow for Dedicated beta, or keep it internal-only until metrics are proven reliable?
3) Approval granularity: is “approval_required_to_enter” sufficient, or do we need separate “approve advance” semantics in v1?
4) Route-scoped gates: do we allow route-level gating in v1, or only pool-level to avoid cardinality + ambiguity?
5) Rollback target: when failure_action=ROLLBACK, is rollback to baseline always safe/defined (e.g., if baseline has been GC’d)?

Notes for Eng implementation alignment
- Keep schema forward-compatible: store unknown gate types/threshold strings without breaking older Console versions.
- Optimistic concurrency required (plan_version).
- Deterministic allocation required (hash key definition TBD; likely tenant_id + stable request key; ensure no PII).

comments: 2025-01-15 (Paula Mendes): Drafted initial stage field list + default gate set. Need SRE input on recommended defaults for queue depth/util thresholds and whether rollback should ever be automatic for latency-only regressions.

2025-01-22 (Sean Gallagher): SRE prefers HOLD on latency/queue/util and only auto-ROLLBACK on sustained 5xx/timeout spikes. Also strongly recommends warmup period before evaluation to avoid first-minute noise; +1 to metrics freshness fail-safe = HOLD.

2025-01-24 (Kenji Nakamura): UX suggestion: keep templates prominent and move per-stage gate customization behind “Advanced settings” to reduce cognitive load. Validation should nudge monotonic % but allow override with warning (for emergency rollbacks).

2025-01-29 (Ethan Park): Control-plane proto can support string thresholds + gate type enums. Relative-to-baseline comparisons are non-trivial; propose v1 uses absolute thresholds and we add baseline-relative in v1.1.

2025-02-03 (Marcus Lin): Approval events must include actor + reason and be exported via audit pipeline. RBAC must gate approve/abort separately from edit. Please ensure API has explicit approval endpoints (no implicit approve via update).

2025-02-06 (Paula Mendes): Updated proposal to split approval_required_to_enter vs approval_required_to_advance. Next: finalize absolute default thresholds per Dedicated tier with SRE and log as decision in PRD.
